comments.body:
Split landed for review as Gerrit 1934.

CONCERN BOUNDARY: blocking vs never-blocking DET checks — the invariant det_floor.py's own docstring already states. The four never-blocking checks (p2_resolution, p3_package_existence, p6_ac_quality, p7_destructive) plus their private regexes moved to a new sibling det_advisory.py; det_floor.py stays the entry module and re-exports them.

CALL-GRAPH EVIDENCE: the moved set is closed — none of the four calls, or is called by, anything that stayed. P2/P3 reach only grounding.refute_absence; P6 is an aggregation hub over lint detectors already living in siblings; P7 calls nothing. The retained checks are the connected ones (P1+P4 share _count_ac_items, P8 uses est_tokens, P5 uses det_lint's graph helpers). Third application of the seam det_lint (P9) and det_clarity (P10/P11) already used.

SIZES: det_floor.py 793 -> 566 (234 lines / 29% headroom under the 800 cap); det_advisory.py 303. Both inside the 200-500 band.

MODULE-OBJECT BINDINGS (what decided which half moves): DET_CHECKS, run_det_floor and est_tokens are monkeypatched on the det_floor module object by test_plan_review.py, test_af77_config_fault.py and test_plan_review_prerequisites{,_heldout}.py; _clarity_score, _count_ac_items and _description_limit are imported from det_floor by name by the lockstep and migration tests. All six are in the RETAINED half, so those patches still reach live code. No moved symbol is monkeypatched anywhere.

CAUGHT BY THE PLAN REVIEW (G6, first pass BLOCK): p6_ac_quality calls vague_hits_in_line, _lint_verify_command and _verify_command_strings as BARE names bound by det_floor's import block — a body-only move would have raised NameError. det_advisory declares those imports itself; det_floor drops them since P6 was their only consumer. The seam test pins this.

PATH-KEYED REGISTRY SWEEP: .github/complexity-baseline.json has NO entry for det_floor.py, so nothing moved a frozen ceiling and nothing went stale — scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check reads new=0 increased=0 stale=0 (checked directly, not just via make lint), and tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py passes. .github/module-size-limit.txt byte-identical to origin/main. The module-size gate and tests/module_size_support.py enumerate by rglob, so the new file needs no registration. tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py _OWNED_FILES/_MARKER_BUDGET needed no change: the module's only config read (_description_limit) stayed, and det_advisory.py carries zero '# read-via:' markers — check_config_ownership.py clean. Prose in registry.py and docs/plan-review-gate.md repointed (comment/doc text only, no assertion touched).

TESTS: RED first — the new seam test failed 18/25 before the split (the 7 passing were premise guards proving the retained half is where the plan claims). GREEN after: 25/25. Zero existing test files modified; the only tests/ addition is the seam test, following the three sibling splits' convention. 1014 passed across every test file that references det_floor. make lint + make typecheck clean.

compiled_state.description:
## Target
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py` — **793 LOC** vs the 800-LOC hard cap: 7 lines of headroom.

## The concern boundary: BLOCKING checks vs NEVER-BLOCKING checks

The module's own docstring already states the invariant this split cuts along: "The only sound,
unambiguous blockers are therefore **P1, P4 (description), P5 (cycle), P8, P10, and P11**.
Everything else is advisory or coverage-only."

That documented boundary is also a real seam in the CALL GRAPH. The four never-blocking checks —
**P2 resolution**, **P3 package-existence**, **P6 AC/DD quality**, **P7 destructive-sniff** — have
ZERO call edges, inbound or outbound, to any other function that stays in `det_floor.py`:

- `p2_resolution` and `p3_package_existence` call only `rebar.grounding.refute_absence` (lazily
  imported) plus their own private extraction regexes `_FILE_REF_RE` / `_PKG_REF_RE`.
- `p6_ac_quality` is a pure aggregation hub over the ALREADY-EXTRACTED advisory-lint siblings:
  `det_operator_attested.ac_item_lines`, `det_clarity.vague_hits_in_line`,
  `det_lint._verify_command_strings` / `_lint_verify_command`,
  `det_operator_attested.operator_evidence_issues`,
  `det_measurement_provenance.provenance_issues`, `det_citation.unbacked_citations`. Moving it puts
  the hub in a module beside its spokes instead of in the floor's core.
- `p7_destructive` calls nothing; it owns `_DESTRUCTIVE_RE` / `_SAFEGUARD_RE` outright.

The checks that STAY are the ones that are actually connected: `p1_readiness_shape` and
`p4_oversize` both call `_count_ac_items`; `p1_readiness_shape` calls `_clarity_score`; `p4_oversize`
calls `_description_limit`; `p8_reviewability` calls `est_tokens`; `p5_task_dag` calls
`det_lint._find_cycle` / `_file_interference`. Cutting between those two sets removes 246 lines
without severing a single existing call edge.

## Established precedent
`det_clarity.py` (P10/P11) and `det_lint.py` (P9 + helpers) were extracted from this module on this
same seam and re-exported from `det_floor.py`. This is the third application of that pattern,
including its cycle-avoidance contract: `from __future__ import annotations` + `TYPE_CHECKING` for
the `DetResult` / `PlanContext` annotations, and a lazy `from .det_floor import DetResult` inside
each function body, so there is no runtime import back into `det_floor`.

## What moves
New module `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_advisory.py` receives these definitions verbatim:
`_FILE_REF_RE`, `p2_resolution`, `_PKG_REF_RE`, `p3_package_existence`, `p6_ac_quality`,
`_DESTRUCTIVE_RE`, `_SAFEGUARD_RE`, `p7_destructive`.

Function bodies alone are not self-contained: `p6_ac_quality` calls `vague_hits_in_line(ln)`,
`_verify_command_strings(ctx)` and `_lint_verify_command(cmd)` as BARE names, bound today by
`det_floor.py`'s module-level import block. So `det_advisory.py` declares its own module-level
imports, mirroring those bindings:

```python
from .det_clarity import vague_hits_in_line
from .det_lint import _lint_verify_command, _verify_command_strings
```

plus `import re`, `from __future__ import annotations`, and `from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any`
with `DetResult` / `PlanContext` under `TYPE_CHECKING`. p6's other dependencies (`det_citation`,
`det_measurement_provenance`, `det_operator_attested`, `rebar._reads`) are already IN-BODY lazy
imports and travel with the body untouched; `p2_resolution` / `p3_package_existence` likewise carry
their in-body `from rebar import grounding`. Each moved function gains one line — the lazy
`from .det_floor import DetResult` — exactly as `det_clarity.p10_verification_presence` and
`det_lint.p9_file_impact_coverage` already do.

Symmetrically, `det_floor.py` DROPS the three imports whose only consumer was `p6_ac_quality`,
while keeping `_find_cycle` / `_file_interference` (used by the retained `p5_task_dag`) and the
`decomposition_state_block` / `veto_undecomposed_g5` re-exports `pass1.py` reaches through it.

`det_floor.py` stays the ENTRY MODULE and dispatcher: it keeps `DetResult`, `PlanContext`,
`est_tokens`, `DET_CHECKS`, `run_det_floor` and the finding/coverage aggregation
(`det_finding_has_subject`, `det_blocking_findings`, `det_advisory_findings`, `det_coverage`), and
re-exports all four moved checks so every existing import point and every `det_floor.<check>`
attribute access keeps resolving unchanged.

## Why the retained half is the half that stays
Three tests bind to the `det_floor` MODULE OBJECT and would silently stop testing anything if their
target moved: `tests/unit/test_plan_review.py` monkeypatches `det_floor.DET_CHECKS`;
`tests/unit/test_af77_config_fault.py` monkeypatches `det_floor.run_det_floor`;
`tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py` and `..._heldout.py` monkeypatch
`sizing.det_floor.est_tokens`. All three targets are in the RETAINED half. `_clarity_score`,
`_count_ac_items` and `_description_limit` are imported by name from `det_floor` by
lockstep/migration tests and also stay. No moved symbol is monkeypatched anywhere; every reference
to a moved symbol is a call through the re-export or a `from ... det_floor import` the re-export
satisfies.

## Sizes
`det_floor.py` 793 -> ~550 (approx 250 lines / 31% headroom); `det_advisory.py` ~300. Both in the
200-500 target band; neither under 100.

## Registry sweep (path-keyed artifacts)
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` — **zero** entries keyed to
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py`, so no moved symbol carries a ceiling and the ratchet
  cannot report `new>0`. Re-verified with `scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`.
- `tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py` `_OWNED_FILES` / `_MARKER_BUDGET` — lists
  `llm/plan_review/det_floor.py`. No config read moves (`_description_limit`, the module's only
  `compose_config` call, stays), so the new module must report zero config-ownership findings and
  zero `# read-via:` markers; verified via `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`.
- `.github/module-size-limit.txt` — NOT touched. The gate and `tests/module_size_support.py` are
  path-agnostic (`rglob`), so the new file needs no registration.
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py` name `det_floor.py` as the
  layer-1 home; prose repointed to name the new sibling. Prose only, no assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `test $(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py) -le 720` exits 0.
- [ ] `test $(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_advisory.py) -ge 100` exits 0.
- [ ] `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_advisory import p2_resolution, p3_package_existence, p6_ac_quality, p7_destructive"` exits 0.
- [ ] `python -c "from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_floor import p2_resolution, p3_package_existence, p6_ac_quality, p7_destructive"` exits 0, proving the re-export preserves the old import point.
- [ ] `python -c "import rebar.llm.plan_review.det_advisory as m; m.vague_hits_in_line; m._lint_verify_command; m._verify_command_strings"` exits 0, proving p6's bare-name dependencies are bound at module level in the new home.
- [ ] `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/` reports no changed test file other than a prose-only docstring repoint.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_plan_review.py tests/unit/test_det_floor_clarity.py tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py tests/unit/test_g5_decomp_det.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites.py tests/unit/test_af77_config_fault.py tests/unit/test_a8e5_det_hygiene_edge.py tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_criteria_heading_collapse.py` exits 0.
- [ ] `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- .github/module-size-limit.txt` exits 0.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0 reporting `new=0 increased=0`.
- [ ] The commit message names the blocking-vs-never-blocking concern boundary as the seam, with its call-graph evidence.

file_impact.reason: Entry module: keeps DetResult/PlanContext/est_tokens/DET_CHECKS/run_det_floor + finding aggregation; re-exports the four moved never-blocking checks
New sibling: receives the never-blocking DET checks P2/P3 (oracle coverage probes) and P6/P7 (advisory lexical sniffs) verbatim
Prose repoint: name the new det_advisory.py sibling alongside det_floor.py
Comment repoint: the P1-P11 home comment names det_advisory.py for P2/P3/P6/P7
